name: Compliance file and permit tracker for small private security companies (operating permit, guard roster, ID cards, insurance and guarantees, arms register)
buyer: Small and mid-size private security companies, now required to be limited-liability companies with minimum capital of 75 SBU. Police counts: 556 with valid permits, 135 in process, 203 expired.
trigger: Ley Orgánica de Vigilancia y Seguridad Privada (RO 9 Feb 2024): operating permit from the Ministerio del Interior, liability and accident insurance, ID cards and uniforms, accreditation and bachillerato for guards, payroll through bank accounts. Defence ministry arms-registry reglamento (July 2025). SERCOP/Interior/IESS/MDT joint inspections of Feb 2026 closed 2 firms for no permit and checked permits, guarantees, payroll, uniform permits and training certificates.
existing: Competitor search in Spanish ('software control guardias empresa de seguridad privada Ecuador cumplimiento ...') found no vendor and no state portal or software. Control looks like inspection and document checks. Guard-tour or ERP vendors not checked.
unchecked: Whether the general reglamento was ever issued; permit renewal cycle (old rule 2 years, industry asked for 4); any electronic Interior portal; reporting frequency (none found); guard-tour or workforce software already sold locally; exact number of firms and willingness to pay (industry says 9 state bodies regulate them); cleaning and manpower agencies not covered.

first_check.duty: Confirmed in force. LOVSP (RO 496, 9 Feb 2024), art. 38: operating permit valid 2 years. The renewal must be filed 90 days before expiry through SICOSEP. The ministry inspects the firm (COSP unit) before renewing. Art. 39 requires civil liability insurance (once the firm contracts arms) and life and personal accident insurance with an updated beneficiary list, each valid at least 2 years. Other requirements: a sworn statement listing contracts, operating staff and arms with valid permits; a 2-year lease; sworn statements of no disqualification (art. 35); and capital of 75 SBU (art. 34). Fees: USD 50, plus USD 200 for each year unrenewed if late. Firms face random inspections, and the Feb 2026 SERCOP/Interior inspections temporarily closed 2 firms with no permit. Not found: whether the general reglamento was issued (due within 90 days of the law), and any monthly or annual reporting duty. The gob.ec procedure page lists none.
first_check.market: Police count (undated, El Comercio): 556 firms with valid permits, 135 in process and 203 expired, about 894 in total, with 68,737 registered guards. Vistazo cites 1,600 registered firms with more than USD 1.1bn in revenue. That makes a few hundred to about 1,600 buyers, a small market.
first_check.competitor: State: SICOSEP, the Interior/Gobierno ministry system for issuing and renewing permits, uploading documents and paying fees. Third-party blogs say it also holds the registry of guard accreditations and training. It handles the filing but does not appear to track expiries across policies, guard credentials and arms permits. Private: none found locally. G4S uses its own in-house CVP app for post and incident control, which it does not sell. Generic international guard time-tracking exists (ShiftFlow) but has no Ecuador compliance features. I did not check local ERP or payroll vendors or the VigiControl app seen on Scribd.
first_check.reason: The duty is real and in force. Ley Orgánica de Vigilancia y Seguridad Privada (RO 496, 9 Feb 2024), art. 38, sets a 2-year operating permit. Renewal must be filed 90 days before expiry through the Interior ministry's SICOSEP system, with both insurance policies, a lease and sworn lists of contracts, guards and arms. Late filers pay USD 200 for each year unrenewed, and the Feb 2026 inspections closed firms. SICOSEP is the free state portal for filing and guard accreditation, but I found no vendor that tracks expiries across the compliance file. Weak points: the main cycle runs every 2 years, the market is small (about 556 to 894 firms on police counts, 1,600 in the trade press), and I could not confirm the general reglamento.

challenge_check.killer: None found. SICOSEP (state, free) handles the permit filing but does not track expiries across documents. Guard-tour apps are not compliance tools. Limits that remain: renewal only every 2 years, a small market of about 400 to 556 firms, and the reglamento apparently never issued.
challenge_check.reason: I found nothing that kills it, but it is weak. SICOSEP, the state system, handles the permit filing itself. The permit renews every 2 years, and the application is due 90 days before expiry (gob.ec page MDI-61, updated June 2025). It requires a list of contracts, guards and arms with valid permits, plus two-year liability and life/accident insurance policies. So the gap is tracking expiries and keeping files ready for inspection, a job a spreadsheet can also do. Guard-tour apps (SoftGuard VigiControl, CGuardPro, ShiftFlow) do not do Ecuadorian compliance, and I found no local vendor. The general reglamento still does not appear to have been issued. The market is small: about 400 to 556 firms, from mostly older counts. There is no periodic reporting, and enforcement is sporadic (SERCOP inspections, Feb 2026).
